question: Does piece (1) (RB3_PROP_POSE_FULL mFinger re-projection break, global) damage the vocalist mic-hand pose? (E6 default-ON blocker)
verdict: RETIRED (blocker not confirmed): piece (1) does NOT damage the vocalist mic-hand pose

evidence.code_level: mic.ikhand has mFinger==NULL (finger=0 in every [PROP_DST] row across OFF/BYPASS/ON) -> the 'if (mFinger && !sFingerBypass && !sPropPoseFull())' re-projection block is SKIPPED identically in OFF and ON. Piece (1) is a provable no-op for the actual mic hand.
evidence.mic_stand: mic_stand.ikhand has mFinger (finger=1). Cross-run dst_from_hand: OFF~81u, FULL-ON~60u. BUT the piece-1-IMMUNE mic.ikhand shifted by the SAME proportion (OFF~75u -> ON~56u, ~-25%), so the shift is shared vocalist animation-phase variance across runs, NOT a piece-1-specific effect. mic_stand reach=0.00 (IK clamp dormant; never skipped/clamped in any run).
evidence.visual: band-closeup-capture.py --member vocals --anchor-ms 26000 OFF vs ON: both verdict=PASS, pinned 6/6, 0 band drops. ON coop_v_n01 shows a coherent leaning singing pose (mic stand visible), no spike-fan / explosion / deformed hand.

caveat: Clears the vocalist mic-chain specifically (the E6(a) A/B). The broader default-ON decision + E6(b) 'scope the global mFinger break OR show it globally harmless' remains coordinator-owned; this lane shows it is harmless for the mic chain.
probe_cap_note: E5 window-share confound is real: the shared per-process [PROP_DST] cap is consumed by the always-over-reaching guitar/drum hands in OFF, starving mic rows even at cap=6000; cap=30000 was needed to capture OFF mic_stand.
